Cuban Salsa is the original form of salsa, originating in Cuba in the 1990’s in Cuba. Cuban Salsa is characterised by it’s circular movement where partners tend to travel around each other (as opposed to Salsa’s linear movement), body isolation, and hip movement. In higher levels, this style can be danced as Rueda, where Cuban salsa moves are called out by a caller, and all partners stand in a circle, creating a symmetrical effect with all partners dancing the same move at the same time.

Cuban Salsa is a partnered dance, but you do not have to bring a partner to dance, you will be paired and rotate partners throughout the night. Comfortable clothes such as activewear and sneakers/dance shoes are recommended. Level 1 is open to all students, while levels 2-3 and Rueda are recommended for students who have already finished all levels below them. Salsa Level 4, Intermediate Partner Work focuses on refining technique and incorporating more complex patterns and styling. Key elements include:
Advanced Turns & Spins: Multiple spins and intricate turn patterns for both the leader and follower.
Complex Partner Combinations: Combining basic steps with advanced moves, like cross-body leads, enchuflas, and inside turns.
Syncopated Footwork: Introduction of syncopated rhythms and footwork variations to add flair.
Improved Connection: Focus on clearer leads and smooth transitions between patterns.
Musicality: Emphasizing the interpretation of the music, with accentuated movements and timing.
At this level, dancers work on perfecting their technique, improving flow, and adding personal style to their partner work.

ClassDescription.Description:
Salsa Level 4, Intermediate Partner Work focuses on refining technique and incorporating more complex patterns and styling. Key elements include:
Advanced Turns & Spins: Multiple spins and intricate turn patterns for both the leader and follower.
Complex Partner Combinations: Combining basic steps with advanced moves, like cross-body leads, enchuflas, and inside turns.
Syncopated Footwork: Introduction of syncopated rhythms and footwork variations to add flair.
Improved Connection: Focus on clearer leads and smooth transitions between patterns.
Musicality: Emphasizing the interpretation of the music, with accentuated movements and timing.
At this level, dancers work on perfecting their technique, improving flow, and adding personal style to their partner work.

ClassDescription.Description:
Sensual Bachata is a dynamic subgenre of Bachata, born in Spain about 15 years ago. It takes the Bachata basics we know and extends them, with longer movements and isolations, with a cornerstone in fluid, whole body stylistic movements and body isolations. In this style connection, fluidity and styling are key, all which are explored across our styling and partnerwork classes.
Sensual Bachata is a partnered dance, with our styling class being taught solo focused on styling and our technique class focusing on partnerwork, fluidity and connection, but you do not have to bring a partner to dance, you will be paired and rotate partners throughout the night. Comfortable clothes such as activewear and sneakers/dance shoes are recommended. Both of these classes are Open Classes, ideal for students who have already completed Level 1 Bachata and are converting this knowledge to Sensual Bachata. If you are a beginner and would like to start learning, you can look instead for Bachata Level 1.

Body Isolations: Practicing isolations, particularly in the chest, hips, and shoulders, to create a dynamic and expressive style.
Posture & Groove: Focusing on maintaining proper posture while staying relaxed, allowing for a natural groove and flow.
Rhythm & Timing: Understanding the music’s beat and timing to keep movements synchronized with the reggaeton rhythm.
At this level, dancers build confidence in their basic technique and begin to express the music through their body movements.

Salsa On2/Mambo is a style of music and dance, originating in Cuba in the 1940’s and popularised in New York city in the 1980’s. Mambo is a partnered dance similar to Salsa, but is characterised by starting on the second beat of the music, and incorporating lots of swivels, spins and rhythmic moves.
It is a partnered dance, but you do not have to bring a partner to dance, you will be paired and rotate partners throughout the night. Comfortable clothes such as activewear and sneakers/dance shoes are recommended.
The Conversion Course will take your knowledge of On1 Salsa and convert it to the Mambo On2 timing, and is recommended for students who have completed at least Salsa Level 1.
The On2 Intermediate level is recommended for students who have done Mambo level 1 or the Conversion Course before.
If you are a beginner and would like to start learning, you can look instead for Salsa Level 1 or Cuban Salsa Level 1.

**This class takes the combos you learned in Level 1 and levels them up with added complexity, smoother transitions, and sharper technique. Perfect for dancers ready to push their skills and feel more confident on the social dance floor!**
Salsa, or Linear/LA Salsa, is the most popular type of Salsa, a well known Latin Dance originating in Cuba in the 1990’s in Cuba, and moulded into the style we recognise today by Francisco, Luis and Johnny Vazquez in LA in the early 2000’s. Linear/LA Salsa is characterised by it’s the linear movements of the follow, danced on the first beat of the music, and incorporating fun partner-work and speedy footwork in solo shines.

Salsa is a partnered dance, but you do not have to bring a partner to dance, you will be paired and rotate partners throughout the night. Comfortable clothes such as activewear and sneakers/dance shoes are recommended. Level 1 is open to all students, while levels 2-6 are recommended for students who have already finished all levels below them. If you have danced Salsa at another studio and are unsure which level to start in, you are more than welcome to talk to a staff member via phone, email, or at reception, or start using our $20 one week trial for new students and try a couple of levels above/below the level you think you would be to get started, and go from there.
